question: x, y and z are distinct prime numbers where x < y < z. If x + y + z = 70, then what is the value of z ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of three prime numbers is even (70), so one of the primes must be the only even prime, which is 2.

Since x [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x, y, z are distinct primes; x [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Even and Odd Prime Property

The number 2 is the only even prime number. All other prime numbers are odd. The sum of three odd numbers is always odd.

Parity of Sums

Sum of 3 numbers = Even ⇒ One is even and two are odd, OR all three are even. Since only one even prime exists, the first case applies.

Goldbach's Conjecture (Related)

Every even integer greater than 2 can be expressed as the sum of two prime numbers (e.g., 68 = 31 + 37).</p
